battle.name: 劉霸道起義
battle.theater: 山東濟北郡鄒平長白山
battle.brief: 隋大業七年（611年），齊州鄒平人劉霸道殺牛起事，旬日聚眾數千，敗於王薄後退保長白山，眾至數萬反隸其下；後攻鄒、范二縣，大破泰山郡守陳馳官軍。九年會竇建德於樂安郡，遂附夏軍受封宋公。卡面秦弩屬戰國形制，與本役相隔八百餘年，不會現於山東；義軍以鄉民刀矛弓弩應戰，隋軍以郡兵結陣圍剿。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場起義是隋末北方亂局中最早一批鄉里武裝之一，交戰的一方是隋朝。隋煬帝楊廣在大業七年（611年）下令山東、河北諸州郡發兵鎮壓，郡兵、州兵與臨時召集的鄉兵由郡守、州刺史就地指揮：這些兵員多為本地農戶，器械自備、編制鬆散，平日用來捕盜守土，一旦大批被抽調北上之後便再也回不來；關鍵時刻朝廷再遣中央行軍大將率關中精兵入關東，麴義真便是奉命東來討平劉霸道與竇建德的主將。另一方是山東起義軍：劉霸道原是濟北郡鄒平的鄉民，殺牛起事後旬日聚眾數千，靠的是同鄉、姻親與鄰里自備的農具、柴刀與弓弩；先後與王薄、孫安祖等部匯合，人數增至數萬，連營於濟北郡長白山下。義軍沒有固定編制與旗號，誰的兵多誰就居中，劉霸道人數多於王薄便受其節制，後來與竇建德合兵時人數近於其半，又改為竇建德的部將，竇建德稱夏王之後封他為宋公。所以整場衝突並不只發生在劉霸道與隋軍之間，也牽動山東、河北、河南三地的郡兵、鄉兵與流民，是隋末「郡兵反噬中央」這一型態最早的樣本之一。
countriesEn: This rising was one of the earliest bodies of county militia formed by village communities in the northern breakdown that ended the Sui dynasty. One side was the Sui state itself. In the seventh year of Daye (611) the Emperor Yang Guang ordered the prefectures and counties of Shandong and Hebei to raise troops for the suppression, and the county troops, commandery troops and hastily summoned village militia were commanded on the spot by the prefect and the governor: these men were mostly local farmers who brought their own weapons and kept a loose organisation, useful for catching bandits and holding the local ground, but never able to return once a great number of them had been sent north. At the decisive moment the court sent a general of the central army with the picked troops of Guanzhong into eastern China, and Qu Yizhen was the commander charged with putting down both Liu BazDao and Dou Jiande. The other side was the rebel army of Shandong. Liu BazDao was a villager of Zouping in the Jibei commandery; after killing a bull to feed his followers he drew several thousand men within ten days, using the farm tools, billhooks and bows that his kinsmen and neighbours had brought with them. He joined up in turn with the bands of Wang Bo and Sun Anzu, his numbers grew to several tens of thousands, and he encamped below Mount Changbai in the Jibei commandery. The rebels had no fixed establishment and no banner of their own: whoever had the most men stood at the centre, and since Liu BazDao outnumbered Wang Bo he came under Wang Bo's command, and when he later joined Dou Jiande, with his force roughly half of Dou's, he became Dou's general instead, receiving the title of Duke of Song after Dou Jiande proclaimed himself King of Xia. The conflict therefore did not run between Liu BazDao and the Sui army alone; it drew the county troops, village militia and refugees of Shandong, Hebei and Henan into the same war, and it is one of the earliest examples of the pattern in which the Sui's own county levies turned against the centre.
people: 劉霸道是起義的發動者，濟北郡鄒平人，家境貧寒，起事之前只是鄉里小民。傳記說他起初連一頭牛都捨不得殺，兒子想吃牛舌而不得，父子為此爭執，最後他終於殺牛饗眾，旬日之間聚起數千鄉勇，隨即裹挾鄰里攻打附近的鄉里與縣邑。真正在山東最早打出聲名的是王薄：劉霸道初起兵時曾敗於王薄之手，退保長白山，待人數聚到數萬，眾望所歸反過來使劉霸道歸屬於王薄，兩部合為一軍，於是名在王薄、實在劉霸道。與他們同時在山東起兵的還有孫安祖，劫掠為生，後來敗於隋將張須陀之手，說明隋廷在地方上確有能戰之將，並非全無應付之力。隋方值得記名的是泰山郡守陳馳，率郡兵迎戰劉霸道而被大破、斬首數千級；以及大將軍麴義真，奉命率關中兵東來討平劉、竇兩部，一度攻堅不下。竇建德則是劉霸道後期最重要的合作者，樂安郡會師之後以夏王自居，劉霸道受封宋公；竇建德敗亡後，劉霸道的兒子劉季隨之歸降唐朝。劉霸道本人的結局在傳記中相當模糊，諸說並存，或云隨軍轉戰河北，或云在戰亂中病卒，無法斷定。
peopleEn: Liu BazDao was the man who set the rising in motion. He was a villager of Zouping in the Jibei commandery, poor, and until the rising began he was only a common man of his village. The record says that at first he could not bring himself to kill even a single bull; his son wanted a slice of ox tongue and was refused, and the two quarrelled over it, until in the end Liu killed the bull and fed the crowd with it, gathering several thousand of the village youths within ten days and then sweeping up the neighbourhood to attack the surrounding villages and market towns. The man who first made a name in Shandong was Wang Bo. Liu BazDao was defeated by him at the beginning of the rising and retired to Mount Changbai; once his numbers had grown to several tens of thousands the balance tipped the other way, and Liu came under Wang Bo's command instead, the two bands merging into one host with the name in Wang Bo and the substance in Liu BazDao. Sun Anzu was raising a band in Shandong at the same time, living by plunder, and was later defeated by the Sui general Zhang Xutuo, which shows that the court did have competent commanders on the ground and was not wholly helpless. On the Sui side the name worth recording is Chen Chi, governor of Mount Tai, whose county troops met Liu BazDao and were badly beaten, with several thousand enemy heads taken; and the general Qu Yizhen, sent with troops from Guanzhong to put down the armies of Liu and Dou, who could not take the mountain positions. Dou Jiande was the most important partner of Liu BazDao in the later phase: after the meeting in the Lean commandery he proclaimed himself King of Xia, and Liu BazDao was made Duke of Song. When Dou Jiande's cause collapsed, Liu BazDao's son Liu Ji went over to the Tang with him. The fate of Liu BazDao himself is very obscure in the sources and the accounts differ: some have him continuing the campaign in Hebei, others have him dying of illness amid the fighting, and it cannot be settled.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩屬戰國時期的弩形：木製弩身配銅或鐵製弩機，扣下機牙時先把弓弦的拉力儲存起來，射手只須壓機，射程遠、動作快，更妙在它把瞄準與發射分成兩步，讓守城的一方可以把射擊的節奏交給受過訓練的弩手而不是靠臂力的弓手。對本場起義而言，這件卡面兵器並不在場：秦弩的形制在漢代已被更強的弩機取代，魏晉南北朝以至隋代，軍中通行的是帶鋼鐵機件的各式弩，兵書所記的擘弓、機弩、連弩之類名目即屬此類，隋軍在山東作戰靠的就是弩手列陣、居高臨下覆蓋城牆與道路，以及在守城時以弩壓制逼近牆下的攻者。起義軍一方則是典型鄉民裝備：鍬、叉、柴刀、木槊、柴槍與鄉間獵弓，許多人是第一次上陣；也有從郡兵、州兵手中繳得的皮甲、櫜弓與環首刀，數量有限，騎兵更少，多靠劫奪驛馬與農畜充當坐騎與負重畜力。隋軍的攻城與野戰器械包括雲梯、撞車、櫓車、投石機與拒馬，並在要道設營壘、斷糧道。左右戰局的其實不是裝備而是糧食：義軍靠就食於鄉里，隋軍遠道而來卻遇上被徵發一空的府庫，只能靠就地徵發與搶掠維持軍用。
kitsEn: The Chinese crossbow on the card is a crossbow of the Warring States type: a wooden stock with a bronze or iron trigger mechanism, which stores the strain of the bowstring when the release is cocked so that the archer need only press the lever. Its range is long, its rate of fire is fast, and its real merit is that it separates aiming from loosing, so that a defending side can hand the rhythm of its shooting to trained crossbowmen rather than to archers whose strength gives out. As for this rising, the weapon on the card was not present: the form of the Qin crossbow had already been superseded by stronger mechanisms in the Han, and from the Wei, Jin and the northern and southern dynasties down to the Sui the armies used crossbows fitted with iron and steel parts, the crossbow types recorded in the military manuals under such names as the powerful drawn bow, the mechanism crossbow and the repeating crossbow. The Sui troops operating in Shandong relied on crossbowmen drawn up in line to cover the walls and the roads from high ground, and on crossbows to pin attackers against the foot of a defended wall. The rebels, by contrast, carried the kit of village communities: spades, forks, billhooks, wooden spear-shafts, cudgels and the hunting bows of the countryside, and many of them saw their first battle there. They had also taken some leather armour, gourd bows and ring-pommel sabres from county and commandery troops, but the quantity was small, and cavalry was rarer still, their mounts and beasts of burden being taken from the post-horses and farm animals they seized. The Sui siege and field train included scaling ladders, battering rams, mantlets, stone-throwers and barricades, and it established entrenched camps on the main roads to cut the rebels' supplies. What decided the war was not the weapons but the food: the insurgents lived off the country they moved through, while the Sui army, arriving from far away, found the granaries already emptied by conscription and had to live on requisition and plunder.
tactics: 起義軍的戰法可以歸納為四點。第一是快：劉霸道起兵旬日即聚數千，靠的是鄉里同時響應、官府反應未及，走到哪裡就裹挾哪裡的鄉民與糧食。第二是據山：長白山在濟北郡鄒平之南，山勢不高但林藪叢雜，便於設營、藏兵與轉移，敗退之後劉霸道退保此處重整，再以人數壓過王薄。第三是以襲擊代替攻城：鄒縣、范縣都是縣級小城，守軍不多，義軍多在夜裡或清晨猝然掩至，奪門而入、捋走府庫與人口，隨即轉向別處，不與官軍主力硬拼。第四是分合：與王薄合兵時劉霸道交出指揮，與竇建德會師又改為附屬，說明山東義軍始終靠聯盟而非編制作戰。隋軍的戰法則是官軍式的穩紮穩打：先以郡兵結陣自保、以城池為依托，逐次集結中央行軍大軍與關中精兵，再圖進剿；麴義真討劉霸道時屢攻不克，反映出郡兵防禦得法、義軍依山固守的一面；而張須陀在山東以精騎快速打擊流動的小股義軍、屢破孫安祖等部，則是另一種成功的做法：不停留、不攻城、不糾纏，以速度壓制速度。雙方的勝負判準也因此不同：義軍要的是能否持續聚人、能否奪到糧食，隋軍要的是能否把流竄的隊伍釘在一處。
tacticsEn: The conduct of the insurgents can be reduced to four points. First, speed: Liu BazDao drew several thousand men within ten days because a whole village neighbourhood rose at once, before the authorities had reacted, and wherever the column went it absorbed the villagers and the grain it passed. Second, the mountain: Mount Changbai lies south of Zouping in the Jibei commandery, and although the hill is not high its woods and scrub make it a good place to pitch camp, hide troops and shift position, so after his defeat Liu BazDao retired there, reorganised, and then outnumbered Wang Bo. Third, raids in place of sieges: Zouping county and Fan county were small walled towns with few defenders, and the rebels generally came on them suddenly in the night or at first light, forced the gate, carried off the stores and the people, and moved on elsewhere rather than stand and fight the Sui main force. Fourth, division and coalition: when he joined Wang Bo Liu BazDao handed over the command, and when he met Dou Jiande he became a subordinate instead, which shows that the Shandong insurgents fought as a coalition of leaders rather than as an army with a constitution. The Sui method, by contrast, was the textbook way of a regular army: the county troops first closed ranks and held the cities, the central field army and the picked troops of Guanzhong were concentrated by stages, and only then was the advance undertaken. Qu Yizhen's failure to take Liu BazDao reflects the soundness of the county defence and the insurgents' use of the hill; Zhang Xutuo's repeated destruction of small roving bands such as Sun Anzu's in Shandong was the other successful method: he never stopped, never sat down before a city and never let himself be drawn into a prolonged engagement, using speed against speed. The tests of success therefore differed on the two sides: for the rebels it was whether they could keep gathering men and seize food, for the Sui it was whether they could pin down a force that never stood still.
data: 史籍留下的數字有限，可以確定的與只能推測的須分開來看。一、可確定的：劉霸道起兵旬日聚眾數千；後與王薄合軍時眾至數萬，連營長白山；劉霸道人數多於王薄，故隸屬於王薄；破鄒、范二縣後與泰山郡守陳馳的官軍戰，斬首數千級；樂安郡會師時劉霸道人馬數萬，竇建德兵未滿十萬，劉霸道遂附屬於竇建德並受封宋公。二、可作背景的：隋大業七年（611年）朝廷大舉募兵、準備征高句麗，兵眾號稱百十三萬，役使遍及山東河北，男子不滿二十歲亦被編入軍伍；此役是劉霸道起事最直接的壓力來源，也說明此役不是孤立事件而是徵役體系崩潰的徵兆；大業八年（612年）隋軍再徵大軍北征，遼東戰敗，役卒死傷以數十萬計，山東河北的起義隨之層出不窮。三、必須保留的：劉霸道的兵員數在不到兩年內由數千增至數萬，數字出自不同史源，統計口徑不一，諸說並存；所謂斬首數千只是斬獲數，並不等於官軍全軍覆沒；起義延續到何年、劉霸道卒年與死因，傳記說法不一，較穩妥的說法是他自大業九年附屬竇建德之後便退居其麾下不再單獨記事。距離上，鄒平、長白山、鄒縣、范縣、泰山郡治分屬今山東鄒平、禹城、泰安一帶，相距多在數十里至百里之間，義軍主力始終在濟北、齊州、泰山三郡的接合部活動。
dataEn: The records preserve few figures, and what can be asserted must be separated from what can only be guessed. First, what can be asserted: Liu BazDao gathered several thousand men within ten days of the rising; when his force merged with Wang Bo's the host numbered several tens of thousands, encamped below Mount Changbai; since Liu outnumbered Wang he came under Wang's command; after taking the two counties of Zouping and Fan he fought the troops of Chen Chi, governor of Mount Tai, and took several thousand heads; and at the meeting in the Lean commandery Liu had several tens of thousands of men and horses against Dou Jiande's not quite a hundred thousand, whereupon Liu became a subordinate of Dou Jiande and was made Duke of Song. Second, what serves as background: in the seventh year of Daye (611) the court raised a great army to invade Goguryeo, the host being put at one hundred and thirteen thousand men, and the levies fell hardest on Shandong and Hebei, with males under twenty years of age being taken into the ranks. That mobilisation was the immediate pressure behind Liu BazDao's rising and shows that the rising was not an isolated event but a symptom of the coming apart of the whole conscription system; in the eighth year of Daye (612) the court raised another great army for the northern campaign, was beaten in Liaodong, and lost a number of its men counted in tens of thousands, after which risings in Shandong and Hebei followed one another. Third, what must be hedged: Liu BazDao's numbers rose from several thousand to several tens of thousands in under two years, the figures come from different sources with different conventions of counting, and the accounts differ; the 'several thousand heads taken' is a tally of heads, not a statement that the Sui force was destroyed; the year in which the rising ended, the year and manner of Liu BazDao's death are given variously, and the safest statement is that from the ninth year of Daye, when he became a subordinate of Dou Jiande, he ceased to be separately recorded. As for distance, Zouping, Mount Changbai, the county seats of Zouping and Fan, and the seat of the Mount Tai commandery lie in what are now Zouping, Yucheng and Tai'an in Shandong, mostly from several tens of li to a hundred li apart, and the rebel main body operated throughout in the junction of the three commanderies of Jibei, Qizhou and Mount Tai.
cause: 要理解這場起義，得從隋朝大業年間的徵役說起。隋煬帝即位之後，北伐突厥、西巡張掖、營造東都與顯仁宮、脩築榆塞，役使與轉運幾乎年年不斷；大業六年（610年）起連年水旱，饑餓遍及河北河南，而百姓的租調與力役一項未減。大業七年（611年），朝廷在山東、河北、黎陽諸處括募兵丁，準備大舉征高句麗，役使百十三萬之眾，男子不滿二十歲者也被編入軍伍，於是齊州、濟北一帶的鄉民整村整戶地離開田里。劉霸道起義的直接背景，就是這套徵發體系落到鄉村之後的樣子：人被拉去當兵或充夫役，田地無人耕種，郡縣官吏照常催督租調與雜役，鄉民既無力繳納也無從申辯。導火線通常記在劉霸道與其子的一次口角上——一條牛舌之爭——牛在饑荒年份是鄉民最貴重的家產，平時連殺牛都捨不得，起兵時殺牛饗眾便是把平日積壓的不平一次宣洩出來。地方秩序也已瀕臨崩潰：郡縣的鄉兵本該是國家用來壓制叛亂的力量，但徵兵愈多，鄉兵愈多，器械與糧秣愈缺，於是郡兵本身成了最容易被裹挾的武裝；同一時期山東已有王薄、孫安祖等部起事，起義之間互相呼應，遂成燎原之勢。
causeEn: To understand this rising one has to begin with the levies of the Daye era. After Yang Guang took the throne there were campaigns against the Turks, tours of inspection to Zhangye, the building of the eastern capital and of the Xianren Palace, and the raising of the Yu frontier wall, with labour service and transport demanded year upon year; from the sixth year of Daye (610) there were successive floods and droughts and hunger spread across northern Henan and Hebei, while the rent, the tribute and the miscellaneous levies charged on the people were not reduced by one single measure. In the seventh year of Daye (611) the court searched out and mustered levies in Shandong, Hebei and Liyang in preparation for the great invasion of Goguryeo, calling up a host of one hundred and thirteen thousand and taking males under twenty into the ranks, so that in the districts of Qizhou and Jibei whole households left the fields. The immediate background of Liu BazDao's rising is what that system of conscription looked like once it reached the villages: the men were taken off to be soldiers or porters, the fields went untended, the county officials continued to press for rent and levies as before, and the villagers had neither the means to pay nor a channel of appeal. The spark is usually placed in a quarrel between Liu BazDao and his son over a strip of ox tongue: in a year of famine the ox was the most valuable beast a villager owned, and to kill one at all was unthinkable in normal times, so killing the bull to feed the crowd was the discharge of a grievance long stored up. The local order was already close to collapse: the village troops of the commanderies and counties existed precisely to suppress rebellion, but the more men were conscripted, the more village troops there were, and the more their arms and supplies fell short, so that the county levies themselves became the armed bodies easiest to carry over into mutiny. In the same years Wang Bo and Sun Anzu had already risen in Shandong, the risings answered one another, and the thing spread like fire in the dry grass.
impact: 劉霸道起義本身的壽命不長，但它在隋末亂局中的位置極為關鍵，因為它把鄉民起兵、郡兵崩解、州郡失守這一連鎖反應第一次完整地演了一遍。義軍攻鄒、范兩縣時地方郡兵幾乎沒有作出像樣的抵抗，說明隋朝的邊防與地方守備在大量兵員被抽調往東北之後已經只剩下空殼；隋廷每一次派中央大將出關鎮壓，都只是把叛軍從一個郡趕到另一個郡，反而使更多郡縣的武裝被攤薄。劉霸道的部眾後來整建制地併入竇建德，竇建德在樂安郡一帶集結山東、河北兩地的流民與散兵，一度擁眾數十萬，成為唐初統一北方的主要對手之一；竇建德降唐之後，其部眾與河北山東的豪強、寺院武裝同樣成了唐朝必須安撫或消化的對象。可以確定的是，李世民在河北與山東用兵時所面對的對手，已經不再是隋朝那些吃俸祿的官軍，而是已經在地方上站住腳、有地盤、有糧道、有騎兵的武裝集團。劉霸道的兒子劉季隨竇建德降唐並受唐廷授職，說明唐初對這些起義首領採取的是收編而非誅殺的政策，此後更被用於招撫河北的劉黑闥、江南的沈法興等人。另一層次值得留意的是，劉霸道與王薄、竇建德之間的聯盟方式——以人數決定指揮權——成為隋末山東義軍的通行規則，也說明當時的所謂聯軍並無制度可言，全靠首領之間的私人信用維持，一旦其中一人失敗或獨強，聯盟就會重新洗牌。
impactEn: The rising of Liu BazDao did not last long, but its place in the final collapse of the Sui is of the first importance, because it was the first time the chain reaction of village rising, county troops breaking up and commanderies falling away had been played through in full. When the rebels took the two counties of Zouping and Fan, the local county troops put up almost no serious resistance, which shows that the frontier and the local defence of the Sui, after so many of their men had been drawn off to the north-east, were down to an empty shell; every time the court sent a general of the central army out of the pass to suppress the rising it merely drove the rebels from one commandery to the next, and thinned out the armed strength of more commanderies in the process. Liu BazDao's host was later absorbed wholesale into Dou Jiande's, and Dou gathered the refugees and scattered fighting men of Shandong and Hebei about the Lean commandery and at one point claimed a host of several hundred thousand, becoming one of the principal opponents of Tang unification in the north; after Dou Jiande's surrender his men, together with the armed households of the great families and of the monasteries in Hebei and Shandong, became in turn objects that the Tang had to pacify or absorb. What is certain is that when Li Shimin campaigned in Hebei and in Shandong he no longer faced the Sui's salaried officials but armed groups that had established themselves locally, with territory, with supply lines and with cavalry. Liu BazDao's son Liu Ji went over to the Tang with Dou Jiande and was given office there, which shows that the early Tang policy towards rebel leaders was to absorb rather than to destroy them; the same policy was later used to win over Liu Heitao in Hebei and Shen Faxing in Jiangnan. Another point worth remarking is the way in which Liu BazDao, Wang Bo and Dou Jiande formed their coalitions: command followed the numbers. That became the working rule of the Shandong insurgents in the late Sui, and it shows that the leagues of that time had nothing of institution about them, being held together entirely by the personal credit of their leaders; as soon as one of them failed or grew strong on his own, the coalition was shuffled again.
result: 就大業七年（611年）這一年而言，劉霸道的結果是旗號得立、隊伍得壯、本人卻沒有成為最後的贏家。起兵之初他以旬日數千之眾在鄒平打出旗號，一度敗於王薄、退保長白山，靠人數增加重新取得主動，繼而攻破鄒、范兩縣、大破泰山郡守陳馳的郡兵，一度進逼泰山郡治，這是劉霸道軍勢的頂點。此後他的隊伍並沒有被消滅，而是整體併入更大的聯軍：大業九年（613年）在樂安郡與竇建德會師，劉霸道人馬數萬，竇建德兵未滿十萬，劉霸道自此歸屬竇建德，被封為宋公，河北山東一帶的戰局改由竇建德主政。隋廷則在麴義真等大將的鎮壓下一度切斷了劉霸道與王薄的聯繫，把起義壓回山東山中；但山東的亂局並未因此結束，反而在竇建德、杜伏威等部接連興起之後被推得更遠。劉霸道本人的結局在傳記中相當模糊，較常見的說法是他隨竇建德轉戰河北，於竇建德敗亡前後病卒或憂鬱而終，其子劉季則隨竇建德降唐並受授武職。若以整場起義的時間跨度計，自611年五月起事到歸附竇建德，劉霸道作為獨立首領的活動前後不過兩年；但正是這兩年，把隋朝在山東的郡縣防務徹底打散，也讓山東的鄉民武裝第一次成建制地站到隋軍的對面，河北的竇建德才有號召山東兵源的資本——這場起義最終的結果，是隋朝平掉了一個名字，卻留下一整片可以招兵的鄉村。
resultEn: For the year 611 itself the outcome of Liu BazDao's rising was this: the banner was raised, the force was made, but the man himself did not end up the winner. At the outset he put up a banner at Zouping with several thousand men drawn within ten days; he was defeated once by Wang Bo and retired to Mount Changbai, recovered the initiative as his numbers grew, then took the two counties of Zouping and Fan and broke the county troops of Chen Chi, governor of Mount Tai, pressing at one point up to the seat of the Mount Tai commandery; that was the high point of his fortunes. His host was not destroyed afterwards but was absorbed whole into a larger coalition: in the ninth year of Daye (613) he met Dou Jiande in the Lean commandery, several tens of thousands of men and horses against Dou's not quite a hundred thousand, and from that point Liu BazDao belonged to Dou Jiande and was made Duke of Song, and the conduct of the war in Hebei and Shandong passed to Dou. The Sui court, through generals such as Qu Yizhen, for a time cut Liu BazDao off from Wang Bo and pressed the rising back into the hills of Shandong; but the disorder in Shandong did not end there and was pushed further out still as the bands of Dou Jiande, Du Fuwei and others rose in turn. The fate of Liu BazDao himself is very obscure in the sources; the account most often given is that he campaigned in Hebei with Dou Jiande and died of illness or of despair around the time Dou's cause collapsed, while his son Liu Ji went over to the Tang with Dou and was given a military command. Counting the whole span of the rising, from the outbreak in the fifth month of 611 to his submission to Dou Jiande, Liu BazDao's career as an independent leader lasted no more than two years. But it was those two years that broke the Sui county defence in Shandong apart, and they were the first time the village armed men of Shandong stood in formed bodies against a Sui army; only then did Dou Jiande in Hebei have the material to call in the manpower of Shandong. The final result of this rising was that the Sui removed a name while leaving behind a whole countryside that could be recruited from.
